question: Which finding, if true, would most strongly support the conclusion reached by Alegado and her colleagues? The biologist Rosanna Alegado proposes that figuring out why Salpingoeca rosetta—a single-celled organism that is the closest living relative of animals—occasionally assembles into cell colonies could reveal how multicellular life arose from single-celled ancestors. Together with her colleagues, Alegado reviewed findings from numerous studies of how S. rosetta reacts to the presence of bacteria (other single-celled organisms), among them Jongsik Chun's research on Algoriphagus mannitolivorans and Ingrid Brettar's research on Aquiflexum balticum. The team concluded that A. mannitolivorans, rather than A. balticum, was more likely to have contributed to the origin of multicellular organisms.
option a: Colonies of S. rosetta formed in both Chun's and Brettar's experiments.
option b: Colonies of S. rosetta formed in neither Chun's nor Brettar's experiments.
option c: Colonies of S. rosetta formed in Chun's experiment but not in Brettar's.
option d: Colonies of S. rosetta formed in Brettar's experiment but not in Chun's.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Since Alegado credits Chun's bacterium (A. mannitolivorans), the support is that only Chun's experiment produced S. rosetta colonies.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Cases in which a technology is adopted for a time and then abandoned—like the swift disappearance of bronze tools and weapons that began around 1300 BCE—can shed light on what drives technological change in early societies. Even so, it is often hard to tell whether the vanishing of certain artifacts reflects a genuine cultural shift or simply results from holes in the archaeological record. A collection of gold items—earrings, beads, and the like—unearthed from Bronze Age and Iron Age sites such as Simagre, Karmir Blur, and other places across the Caucasus shows a sharp drop in the overall count of gold artifacts beginning roughly 1500 BCE at some locations. This drop probably reflects a real cultural change, given that ______
option a: there is a positive correlation between how many gold objects turn up at Caucasus sites and how far each site lies from nearby gold sources, such as deposits of gold ore.
option b: the ratio of gold objects to other recovered types of objects is considerably higher at Simagre than at Karmir Blur, even though the two sites are located close together.
option c: far fewer gold objects predating 1500 BCE have been recovered from Caucasus sites than from comparably old sites located outside the region.
option d: the dataset includes a far greater number of Caucasus sites dating from after 1500 BCE than sites dating from before 1500 BCE.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If more post-1500 BCE sites were sampled yet gold artifacts still declined, the drop is a real change, not a gap in the record.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Encaustic is a method that artists have employed since no later than the fifth century BCE. ______ using heated wax combined with pigments. For an example of the technique, look at Betsy Eby's 2019 piece Wishing Well.
option a: She involves
option b: These involve
option d: They involve
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular subject 'Encaustic' (the technique) requires the singular pronoun-verb 'It involves.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? An office of the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) is located in Seoul, South Korea. You won't, however, spot Interpol agents chasing international criminals through Seoul. Although Interpol can assist with investigations, only South Korean authorities ______ allowed to carry out arrests there.
option a: were being
option b: had been
option d: are
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The surrounding present-tense context calls for the present-tense verb 'are.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? An assault by plant-eating mustard aphids, which are among the cuckoopint plant's most frequent insect predators, ______ to produce proteins that interfere with the aphids' ability to digest their food.
option a: triggering the plant
option b: will trigger the plant
option d: the plant will be triggered
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular subject 'An assault' needs the finite main verb phrase 'will trigger the plant.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In a 2001 article, the law professors Akhil and Vikram Amar argued that the arrangement granting Florida's 30 electoral votes to whichever US presidential candidate wins the most votes from Florida's voters, rather than from all voters, ______ open to reform—provided that states agreed to award their electoral votes to the winner of the national popular vote.
option a: being
option b: are
option d: was
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular subject 'the arrangement/system' takes the singular past-tense verb 'was.'

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The archaeological site of La Venta sits in our home state of Tabasco, Mexico. ______ the ancient Olmec civilization left behind a 19.8-ton stone statue of a human head. In the neighboring state of Veracruz stood another stone statue, this one weighing 25.3 tons.
option a: Therefore,
option b: Similarly,
option d: In other words,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Here' points back to La Venta in Tabasco as the place the statue was left.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? One might expect that Germany's Nordsee One offshore wind farm generates as much energy as land-based wind farms of comparable size. ______ because wind speeds over open water tend to exceed those over land, the turbines at Nordsee One spin faster and produce more energy than the turbines at most land-based farms.
option a: For example,
option b: Actually,
option d: Therefore,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Actually' signals that the expected result is overturned by the facts that follow.

question: The student wants to describe what the band's members wear. Which choice best uses information from the notes to do this? A student has taken these notes: The marching band at Elizabeth City State University (ECSU) is called the Sound of Class. The band's members wear uniforms. The uniforms are blue, gray, and white.
option a: Members of the Sound of Class wear blue, gray, and white uniforms.
option b: ECSU's marching band is called the Sound of Class.
option d: The Sound of Class was founded in the 1930s.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only option A describes the members' clothing, naming the uniform colors.

question: The student wants to highlight a similarity between the two studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: A 2001 study by Wilby and Brown, conducted in a grassland setting in the United Kingdom, found that the presence of plant litter negatively affected seedling emergence. A 2010 study by Clark and Tilman, conducted in a grassland setting in the United States, likewise found that plant litter had a negative effect on seedling emergence.
option a: Over the years, researchers have examined the effect of plant litter on seedling emergence.
option b: Wilby and Brown (2001) found that plant litter in a grassland setting in the United Kingdom had a negative effect on seedling emergence.
option c: In studies by both Wilby and Brown (2001) and Clark and Tilman (2010), the presence of plant litter in a grassland setting was found to have a negative effect on seedling emergence.
option d: Wilby and Brown conducted a study in the United Kingdom, whereas Clark and Tilman's study was conducted in the United States.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Option C names both studies together and states their shared finding, emphasizing the similarity.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to make and support a generalization about silent films made before 1930? Silent films can serve as valuable historical records of their era. Of the silent films produced before 1930, ninety percent are now lost. A film is deemed lost when no surviving copies are known to exist. Oscar Micheaux's 1927 silent film The House Behind the Cedars is lost, as is Henry MacRae's 1925 silent film Ace of Spades. Archives such as the UCLA Film and Television Archive in Los Angeles, California, help preserve some of the surviving films from the 1920s.
option a: The UCLA Film and Television Archive in Los Angeles, California, is one of many archives helping to preserve some of the surviving silent films from the 1920s.
option b: The lost silent films The House Behind the Cedars and Ace of Spades were made by different directors.
option c: The House Behind the Cedars, a film from 1927 by Oscar Micheaux, is now considered lost.
option d: While some have been preserved in archives, many silent films from before 1930--in fact, ninety percent of them--are lost to history.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Option D generalizes that 90 percent of pre-1930 silent films are lost despite some archival preservation.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The Yupno people, who inhabit the remote Finisterre Range of Papua New Guinea, do not measure age and possess no artificial devices (such as clocks) for keeping track of time; this, however, does not mean that the Yupno are ______ time. As Rafael Núñez and his colleagues have recently demonstrated, the Yupno language contains numerous expressions relating to time, such as kalip si ngan, which translates to "a long time ago."
option a: dependent on
option b: meticulous about
option d: inattentive to
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Inattentive to' fits the contrast showing the Yupno actually attend to time through their many temporal expressions.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Scientists recently built a model to forecast how shorter winters will affect the future sizes of mammal populations in US national forests. Unfortunately, when the model is applied to large forests its predictions for large-mammal populations run too high, and when it is applied to small forests its predictions for small-mammal populations run too high. Tuskegee National Forest in Alabama is a small forest, covering fewer than 100,000 acres. If it were used to evaluate the effect of shorter winters on this forest ten years from now, the model would therefore likely ______
option a: exaggerate the effect of shorter winters on large mammals.
option b: reflect factors affecting small mammals other than shorter winters.
option c: overestimate the actual population sizes of small mammals.
option d: ignore the predator-prey relationships between large and small mammals.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Applied to a small forest, the model overpredicts small-mammal populations.

question: The student wants to provide an example of a sky island. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: The Peloncillo Mountains form a mountain range in the southwestern United States. This range is one of the dozens of "sky islands" located in the southwestern US and northwestern Mexico. A sky island is an isolated mountain range whose environment differs sharply from that of the surrounding lowlands. The US Forest Service (USFS) said, "The mountains are 'islands' surrounded by deserts that are 'seas.'" The USFS said, "Each Sky Island is a unique ecosystem."
option a: In the southwestern US and northwestern Mexico, there are dozens of sky islands: isolated mountain ranges whose environments differ drastically from that of the surrounding lowlands.
option b: Sky islands are isolated mountain ranges whose environments differ drastically from that of the surrounding lowlands; as the USFS puts it, "the mountains are 'islands' surrounded by deserts that are 'seas.'"
option c: There are dozens of sky islands in the southwestern US and northwestern Mexico, such as the Peloncillo Mountains.
option d: The USFS considers each of the sky islands, whose environments differ drastically from that of the surrounding lowlands, to be a "unique ecosystem."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Option C offers the Peloncillo Mountains as a concrete example of a sky island.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? A study by Augusta D. Gaspar and Joana Carneiro Pinto found that a bank's corporate social responsibility (CSR) efforts, such as environmental and social campaigns, improve its corporate image. When a bank's marketing strategies mentioned CSR, the favorability scores that study participants assigned tended to ______ the scores that participants assigned when CSR was not mentioned.
option a: replace
option b: identify
option d: disturb
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Exceed' fits the finding that mentioning CSR pushed favorability scores above the no-CSR scores.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "manifest" most nearly mean? The following text is adapted from Virginia Woolf's 1919 novel Night and Day. Katharine is the granddaughter of a celebrated poet.
[Katharine's] descent from [a celebrated poet] was no surprise to her, but matter for satisfaction, until, as the years wore on, certain drawbacks made themselves very manifest. Perhaps it is a little depressing to inherit not lands but an example of intellectual virtue; perhaps the conclusiveness of a great ancestor is a little discouraging to those who run the risk of comparison with him.
option a: Evident
option b: Particular
option d: Complex
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Here 'manifest' means the drawbacks became clearly apparent, i.e., evident.

question:
Which choice best describes data in the table that support the city planner's conclusion?
Ranking of Environmental and Sociocultural Benefits of Urban Agriculture (scale of 1 to 25; 1 = highest)
Social or ecological service | Project leaders | Stakeholders | General public
improvement of social cohesion | 17 | 10 | 9
creation of new forms of recreation | 8 | 2 | 1
provision of habitat for fauna | 13 | 8 | 18
contribution to political fulfillment | 21 | 23 | 24
improvement of physical health | 5 | 4 | 7
Esther Sanyé-Mengual, Kathrin Specht, and their colleagues surveyed three groups of people in Bologna, Italy--leaders of urban agriculture projects, stakeholders in urban agriculture (for instance, food researchers and urban farming associations), and the general public--in order to compare their views on the degree to which urban agriculture contributes to 25 social or ecological services the team had identified. Using these ratings, the researchers ranked the services for each group, with a ranking of 1 meaning that the group perceives urban agriculture as benefiting that service the most. Relying only on the rankings in the table, a Bologna city planner promoting a new urban agriculture project concludes that advertisements directed at project leaders should emphasize the project's benefit to the improvement of physical health.
option a: The contribution to political fulfillment was ranked higher for project leaders than was the improvement of physical health.
option b: The improvement of physical health was ranked higher for project leaders than it was for stakeholders.
option c: The creation of new forms of recreation was ranked lower for project leaders than it was for the general public.
option d: The improvement of physical health was ranked higher for project leaders than were the other four services.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: For project leaders, physical health has the best (highest) rank of the five services, supporting the planner's focus on it.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To write the entry for "pahoehoe"--a term for a kind of lava with a smooth or ropy surface--the editors of Home Ground: A Guide to the American Landscape turned to the essayist Pamela Frierson. For "arroyo," however, they chose the nonfiction ______ author of Adios to the Brushlands.
option a: writer Arturo Longoria
option b: writer, Arturo Longoria,
option d: writer, Arturo Longoria
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No comma precedes the restrictive name, and one comma follows to set off the appositive 'author of Adios to the Brushlands.'

question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text? In his prose poem "Other Things," Alvin Pang pushes back against the idea that prose poetry--a hybrid form pairing prose formatting with figurative language and other conventional poetic devices--must be confined to a single page. Jane Monson is one of many poets and scholars who insist that a prose poem should not run longer than one page, while others favor greater length, welcoming works that span multiple pages. Anthologies reflect this disagreement: although the vast majority of prose poems in such collections run under half a page, The Penguin Book of the Prose Poem (2018) features a notably high proportion of longer pieces.
option a: Some scholars and poets have criticized Pang's poem "Other Things" for exceeding the generally accepted length for prose poems.
option b: The editorial choices of a 2018 anthology are a reflection of the widening acceptance of longer prose poetry.
option c: As seen in a work by Pang and in the greatly differing approaches taken in anthologies, prose poems vary widely in length.
option d: The ideal length for prose poems remains a contested subject among scholars and practitioners of the form.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text's central point is that the proper length of a prose poem is still disputed among poets and scholars.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Allowing the liquid both to keep its structural integrity and to spread with ease, ______
option a: ketchup relies on its non-Newtonian properties for its utility as a consumer product.
option b: a consumer product like ketchup derives its utility from its non-Newtonian properties.
option c: ketchup is a consumer product whose non-Newtonian properties are essential to its utility.
option d: the non-Newtonian properties of ketchup are essential to its utility as a consumer product.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The opening modifier describes the non-Newtonian properties, so those properties must be the subject that follows.
